BOULDER, Colo. — Physicist Jun Ye of the U.S. Department of Commerce’s National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) has been awarded the 2026 Wolf Prize in Physics. The award, often considered the second most prestigious award in the physical sciences, after the Nobel Prize in Physics, cited Ye’s achievement in “transformative, widely applicable advances in the control of ultracold atomic systems.” “Honored and humbled, I wish to express my sincere gratitude to the Wolf Prize Committee,” Ye said. “I am very fortunate to have worked with so many brilliant scientists, from my mentors and close colleagues to the world's best students and postdocs in our lab." Ye has pioneered the development of the world’s most accurate and stable optical atomic clocks, which have unprecedented precision and are paving the way to redefine the international standard for time and frequency measurements. He and his collaborators achieved those record-breaking results using ultrastable lasers and precise control of the interactions between laser-trapped atoms.
